verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要告诉本国的子民说：我使刀剑临到哪一国，那一国的民从他们中间选立一人为守望的。
verses.en: “Son of man, speak to your people,[NOTE:1] and say to them, ‘Suppose I bring a sword against the land, and the people of the land take one man from their borders and make him their watchman.
notes: Heb “sons of your people.”

verses.zh: 他见刀剑临到那地，若吹角警戒众民，
verses.en: He sees the sword coming against the land, blows the trumpet,[NOTE:1] and warns the people,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “shofar,” a ram’s horn rather than a brass instrument (so throughout the chapter).
Sounding the trumpet could warn of imminent danger (Neh 4:18-20; Jer 4:19; Amos 3:6).

verses.zh: 凡听见角声不受警戒的，刀剑若来除灭了他，他的罪（原文是血）就必归到自己的头上。
verses.en: but there is one who hears the sound of the trumpet yet does not heed the warning. Then the sword comes and sweeps him away. He will be responsible for his own death.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his blood will be on his own head.”

verses.zh: 他听见角声，不受警戒，他的罪必归到自己的身上；他若受警戒，便是救了自己的性命。
verses.en: He heard the sound of the trumpet but did not heed the warning, so he is responsible for himself.[NOTE:1] If he had heeded the warning, he would have saved his life.
notes: Heb “his blood will be on him.”

verses.zh: 倘若守望的人见刀剑临到，不吹角，以致民不受警戒，刀剑来杀了他们中间的一个人，他虽然死在罪孽之中，我却要向守望的人讨他丧命的罪（原文是血）。
verses.en: But suppose the watchman sees the sword coming and does not blow the trumpet to warn the people. Then the sword comes and takes one of their lives. He is swept away for his iniquity,[NOTE:1] but I will hold the watchman accountable for that person’s death.’[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “in his punishment.” The phrase “in/for [a person’s] iniquity/punishment” occurs fourteen times in Ezekiel: here and in vv. 8 and 9; 3:18, 19; 4:17; 7:13, 16; 18:17, 18, 19, 20; 24:23; 39:23. The Hebrew word for “iniquity” may also mean the “punishment” for iniquity or “guilt” of iniquity.
Heb “his blood from the hand of the watchman I will seek.”

verses.zh: 「人子啊，我照样立你作以色列家守望的人。所以你要听我口中的话，替我警戒他们。
verses.en: “As for you, son of man, I have made you a watchman[NOTE:1] for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you must warn them on my behalf.
notes: Jeremiah (Jer 6:17) and Habakkuk (Hab 2:1) also served in the role of a watchman.

verses.zh: 我对恶人说：『恶人哪，你必要死！』你―以西结若不开口警戒恶人，使他离开所行的道，这恶人必死在罪孽之中，我却要向你讨他丧命的罪（原文是血）。
verses.en: When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you must certainly die,’[NOTE:1] and you do not warn[NOTE:2] the wicked about his behavior,[NOTE:3] the wicked man will die for his iniquity, but I will hold you accountable for his death.[NOTE:4]
notes: The same expression occurs in Gen 2:17.
Heb “and you do not speak to warn.”
Heb “way.”
Heb “and his blood from your hand I will seek.”

verses.zh: 倘若你警戒恶人转离所行的道，他仍不转离，他必死在罪孽之中，你却救自己脱离了罪。」
verses.en: But if you warn the wicked man to change his behavior,[NOTE:1] and he refuses to change,[NOTE:2] he will die for his iniquity, but you have saved your own life.
notes: Heb “from his way to turn from it.”
Heb “and he does not turn from his way.”

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要对以色列家说：你们常说：『我们的过犯罪恶在我们身上，我们必因此消灭，怎能存活呢？』
verses.en: “And you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, ‘This is what you have said: “Our rebellious acts and our sins have caught up with us,[NOTE:1] and we are wasting away because of them. How then can we live?”’
notes: Heb “(are) upon us.”

verses.zh: 你对他们说，主耶和华说：我指着我的永生起誓，我断不喜悦恶人死亡，惟喜悦恶人转离所行的道而活。以色列家啊，你们转回，转回吧！离开恶道，何必死亡呢？
verses.en: Say to them, ‘As surely as I live, declares the Sovereign Lord, I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but prefer that the wicked change his behavior[NOTE:1] and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil deeds![NOTE:2] Why should you die, O house of Israel?’
notes: Heb “turn from his way.”
Heb “ways.” This same word is translated “behavior” earlier in the verse.

verses.zh: 人子啊，你要对本国的人民说：义人的义，在犯罪之日不能救他；至于恶人的恶，在他转离恶行之日也不能使他倾倒；义人在犯罪之日也不能因他的义存活。
verses.en: “And you, son of man, say to your people,[NOTE:1] ‘The righteousness of the righteous will not deliver him if he rebels.[NOTE:2] As for the wicked, his wickedness will not make him stumble if he turns from it.[NOTE:3] The righteous will not be able to live by his righteousness[NOTE:4] if he sins.’[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the sons of your people.”
Heb “in the day of his rebellion.” The statement envisions a godly person rejecting what is good and becoming sinful. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:247-48.
Heb “and the wickedness of the wicked, he will not stumble in it in the day of his turning from his wickedness.”
Heb “by it.”
Heb “in the day of his sin.”

verses.zh: 我对义人说：『你必定存活！』他若倚靠他的义而作罪孽，他所行的义都不被记念。他必因所作的罪孽死亡。
verses.en: Suppose I tell the righteous that he will certainly live, but he becomes confident in his righteousness and commits iniquity. None of his righteous deeds will be remembered; because of the iniquity he has committed he will die.

verses.zh: 再者，我对恶人说：『你必定死亡！』他若转离他的罪，行正直与合理的事：
verses.en: Suppose I say to the wicked, ‘You must certainly die,’ but he turns from his sin and does what is just and right.

verses.zh: 还人的当头和所抢夺的，遵行生命的律例，不作罪孽，他必定存活，不致死亡。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] returns what was taken in pledge, pays back what he has stolen, and follows the statutes that give life,[NOTE:2] committing no iniquity. He will certainly live—he will not die.
notes: Heb “the wicked one.”
Heb “and in the statutes of life he walks.”

verses.zh: 他所犯的一切罪必不被记念。他行了正直与合理的事，必定存活。
verses.en: None of the sins he has committed will be counted[NOTE:1] against him. He has done what is just and right; he will certainly live.
notes: Heb “remembered.”

verses.zh: 「你本国的子民还说：『主的道不公平。』其实他们的道不公平。
verses.en: “Yet your people[NOTE:1] say, ‘The behavior[NOTE:2] of the Lord is not right,’[NOTE:3] when it is their behavior that is not right.
notes: Heb “the sons of your people.”
Heb “way.”
The Hebrew verb translated “is (not) right” has the basic meaning of “to measure.” For a similar concept, see Ezek 18:25, 29.

verses.zh: 义人转离他的义而作罪孽，就必因此死亡。
verses.en: When a righteous man turns from his godliness and commits iniquity, he will die for it.

verses.zh: 恶人转离他的恶，行正直与合理的事，就必因此存活。
verses.en: When the wicked turns from his sin and does what is just and right, he will live because of it.

verses.zh: 你们还说：『主的道不公平。』以色列家啊，我必按你们各人所行的审判你们。」
verses.en: Yet you say, ‘The behavior of the Lord is not right.’ House of Israel, I will judge each of you according to his behavior.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “ways.”

verses.zh: 我们被掳之后十二年十月初五日，有人从耶路撒冷逃到我这里，说：「城已攻破。」
verses.en: In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month,[NOTE:1] a refugee came to me from Jerusalem[NOTE:2] saying, “The city has been defeated!”[NOTE:3]
notes: January 19, 585 b.c.
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “smitten.”

verses.zh: 逃来的人未到前一日的晚上，耶和华的灵（原文是手）降在我身上，开我的口。到第二日早晨，那人来到我这里，我口就开了，不再缄默。
verses.en: Now the hand of the Lord had been on me[NOTE:1] the evening before the refugee reached me, but the Lord[NOTE:2] opened my mouth by the time the refugee arrived[NOTE:3] in the morning; he opened my mouth and I was able to speak once more.[NOTE:4]
notes: The other occurrences of the phrase “the hand of the Lord” in Ezekiel are in the context of prophetic visions.
Heb “he”; the referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “by the time of the arrival to me.” For clarity the translation specifies the refugee as the one who arrived.
Ezekiel’s God-imposed muteness was lifted (see 3:26).

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，住在以色列荒废之地的人说：『亚伯拉罕独自一人能得这地为业，我们人数众多，这地更是给我们为业的。』
verses.en: “Son of man, the ones living in these ruins in the land of Israel are saying, ‘Abraham was only one man, yet he possessed the land, but we are many; surely the land has been given to us for a possession.’[NOTE:1]
notes: Outside of its seven occurrences in Ezekiel the term translated “possession” appears only in Exod 6:8 and Deut 33:4.

verses.zh: 所以你要对他们说，主耶和华如此说：你们吃带血的物，仰望偶像，并且杀人流血，你们还能得这地为业吗？
verses.en: Therefore say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: You eat the meat with the blood still in it,[NOTE:1] pray to[NOTE:2] your idols, and shed blood. Do you really think you will possess[NOTE:3] the land?
notes: This practice was a violation of Levitical law (see Lev 19:26).
Heb “lift up your eyes.”
Heb “Will you possess?”

verses.zh: 你们倚仗自己的刀剑行可憎的事，人人玷污邻舍的妻，你们还能得这地为业吗？
verses.en: You rely[NOTE:1] on your swords and commit abominable deeds; each of you defiles his neighbor’s wife. Will you possess the land?’
notes: Heb “stand.”

verses.zh: 你要对他们这样说，主耶和华如此说：我指着我的永生起誓，在荒场中的，必倒在刀下；在田野间的，必交给野兽吞吃；在保障和洞里的，必遭瘟疫而死。
verses.en: “This is what you must say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: As surely as I live, those living in the ruins will die[NOTE:1] by the sword, those in the open field I will give to the wild beasts for food, and those who are in the strongholds and caves will die of disease.
notes: Heb “fall.”

verses.zh: 我必使这地荒凉，令人惊骇；她因势力而有的骄傲也必止息。以色列的山都必荒凉，无人经过。
verses.en: I will turn the land into a desolate ruin; her confident pride will come to an end. The mountains of Israel will be so desolate no one will pass through them.

verses.zh: 我因他们所行一切可憎的事使地荒凉，令人惊骇。那时，他们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: Then they will know that I am the Lord when I turn the land into a desolate ruin because of all the abominable deeds they have committed.’[NOTE:1]
notes: The judgments of vv. 27-29 echo the judgments of Lev 26:22, 25.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你本国的子民在墙垣旁边、在房屋门口谈论你。弟兄对弟兄彼此说：『来吧！听听有甚么话从耶和华而出。』
verses.en: “But as for you, son of man, your people[NOTE:1] (who are talking about you by the walls and at the doors of the houses) say to one another,[NOTE:2] ‘Come hear the word that comes[NOTE:3] from the Lord.’
notes: Heb “sons of your people.”
Heb “one to one, a man to his brother.”
Heb “comes out.”

verses.zh: 他们来到你这里如同民来聚会，坐在你面前彷佛是我的民。他们听你的话却不去行；因为他们的口多显爱情，心却追随财利。
verses.en: They come to you in crowds,[NOTE:1] and they sit in front of you as[NOTE:2] my people. They hear your words, but do not obey[NOTE:3] them. For they talk lustfully,[NOTE:4] and their heart is set on[NOTE:5] their own advantage.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “as people come.” Apparently this is an idiom indicating that they come in crowds. See D. I. Block, Ezekiel (NICOT), 2:264.
The word “as” is supplied in the translation.
Heb “do.”
Heb “They do lust with their mouths.”
Heb “goes after.”

The present translation understands the term often used for “unjust gain” in a wider sense, following M. Greenberg, who also notes that the LXX uses a term that can describe either sexual or ritual pollution. See M. Greenberg, Ezekiel (AB), 2:687.

verses.zh: 他们看你如善于奏乐、声音幽雅之人所唱的雅歌，他们听你的话却不去行。
verses.en: Realize[NOTE:1] that to them you are like a sensual song, a beautiful voice, and skilled musician.[NOTE:2] They hear your words, but they do not obey them.[NOTE:3]
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates becoming aware of something and has been translated here as a verb.
Heb “one who makes playing music well.”
Similar responses are found in Isa 29:13; Matt 21:28-32; James 1:22-25.

verses.zh: 看哪，所说的快要应验；应验了，他们就知道在他们中间有了先知。」
verses.en: When all this comes true—and it certainly will[NOTE:1]—then they will know that a prophet was among them.”
notes: Heb “behold, it is coming.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above.
Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Third paragraph, etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Ezekiel 12-24 explains YHWH's reason for His judgment on Judah.

- Ezekiel 25-32 is YHWH's judgments on the surrounding nations.

- Ezekiel 33-39 is the message to the exiles of YHWH's promised restoration.

- Ezekiel 33 is very similar to Ezekiel 18 in its emphasis on individual responsibility (cf. Deut. 24:16; Jer. 31:29-30). In this chapter the
people admit their sin (cf. Ezek. 33:10). This theme of individual responsibility is one major truth of the book of Ezekiel and it begins in Ezek. 3:16-21.

Special Topic: Covenant

- A footnote in the REB Oxford Study Bible, p. 893, asserts that this chapter repates themes given earlier in Ezekiel.

- 33:1-6 from 3:4-11

- 33:7-9 from 3:16-21

- 33:10-20 from 18:1-32

- 33:23-29 from 12:17-20

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:1-6

1And the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 2"Son of
man, speak to the sons of your people and say to them, 'If I bring a sword upon a land, and the people of the land take one man from among them and make him their
watchman, 3and he sees the sword coming upon the land and blows on the trumpet and warns the people, 4then he who hears the sound
of the trumpet and does not take warning, and a sword comes and takes him away, his blood will be on his own head. 5He heard the sound of the
trumpet but did not take warning; his blood will be on himself. But had he taken warning, he would have delivered his life. 6But if the watchman sees the
sword coming and does not blow the trumpet and the people are not warned, and a sword comes and takes a person from them, he is taken away in his iniquity; but his
blood I will require from the watchman's hand.'"

33:1 This phrase is the literary marker for a new prophecy, used many times.

33:2 "Son of man" See full note at Ezek. 2:1.

Special Topic: Son of Man

▣"speak" As so many of Ezekiel's prophecies this one starts out with the command "speak" or
"say" (BDB 180; KB 210, Piel IMPERATIVE).

▣ "to the sons of your people" This is found only in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 3:11; 33:2,12,17,30; 37:18)
and mostly in this chapter.

Special Topic: Sons of. . .(OT)

▣ "If I bring a sword upon a land" This theme is amplified in chapter 21. The word was one of
several items of judgment (sword, famine, plague, wild beasts, e.g. Ezek. 5:17). This would take the readers'/hearers'
minds back to Leviticus 26 or Deuteronomy 27-28.

▣ "watchman" The world translated "watchman" is really a Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE of the VERB
"to look out," "look about" or "spy out" (BDB 859, KB 1044, cf. Ezek. 33:2,6 [twice],7). This is the man who stood on the wall (or in a watchtower) to give an
early warning of coming danger (cf. Ezek. 3:16-21; Isa. 21:4-10; 56:10; Jer. 6:17; Hosea 9:8).

33:3 "he sees the sword coming" The sword is used as imagery for an invading army. In this case it refers to the army of Nebuchadnezzar II of Neo-Babylon.

Special Topic: Kings of Neo-Babylon

▣ "the trumpet" This refers to the sophar (BDB 1051) or ram's horn. It was used both for religious purposes
and and military purposes (cf. Josh. 6:4; 2 Sam. 2:28; 18: 24,25; Ps. 81:3; Joel 2:15; Amos 3:6; Hab. 2:1).

Special Topic: Horns Used By Israel.

▣ "warns" This VERB (BDB 264, KB 265, Hiphil PERFECT with waw)
means "to warn" or possibly from an Aramaic root, "to teach" (cf. Exod. 18:20). It is found in the VERB form only and
predominately in Ezekiel in two forms.

- Hiphil, to warn or caution (cf. Ezek. 3:17,18 [twice],19,20,21 [twice]; 33:3,7,8,9)

- Niphal, to be warned (cf. Ezek. 3:21; 33:4,5 [twice],6)

33:4,6 "his blood will be on his own head. . .but his blood I will require at the watchman's hand" Ezekiel felt the pressure of
speaking YHWH's word to a non-responsive people (as did Isaiah and Jeremiah). In a sense he is defending his message of judgment on Judah.
If he had not spoken, the inhabitants could have blamed him or God for the destruction and death of the nation. But he did speak and they still did
not respond (cf. Isa. 6:9-10).

The word "blood" stands for a person's life (cf. Ezek. 18:13; Lev. 17:11,14).

Special Topic: Blood

▣ "watchman's hand" See Special Topic: Hand

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:7-9

7"Now as for you, son of man, I have appointed you a watchman for the house of Israel; so
you will hear a message from My mouth and give them warning from Me. 8When I say to the wicked, 'O wicked man, you will surely die,' and you
do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity, but his blood I will require from your hand. 9But if you on
your part warn a wicked man to turn from his way and he does not turn from his way, he will die in his iniquity, but you have delivered your life.

33:8 "you will surely die" This is a Hebrew grammatical construction (i.e. INFINITIVE
ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT VERB from the same root, here BDB 559, KB 562),
which denotes emphasis or intensity (same phrase in Gen. 2:17).

- This one is repeated in Ezek. 33:14.

- Another related one (i.e. BDB 310, KB 309, "he will surely live") is found in Ezek. 33:13,15,16.

▣ "that wicked man shall die in his iniquity" This is the message of chapter 18. If one repents,
YHWH will forgive. If one sins and refuses to repent, that one will bear his judgment.

Special Topic: Repentance (OT)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:10-16

10"Now as for you, son of man, say to the house of Israel, 'Thus you have spoken, saying, "Surely
our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we are rotting away in them; how then can we survive?"' 11Say to them, 'As I live!' declares the Lord
God, 'I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked, but rather that the wicked turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your
evil ways! Why then will you die, O house of Israel?' 12And you, son of man, say to your fellow citizens, 'The righteousness of a righteous man will not
deliver him in the day of his transgression, and as for the wickedness of the wicked, he will not stumble because of it in the day when he turns from his wickedness;
whereas a righteous man will not be able to live by his righteousness on the day when he commits sin.' 13When I say to the righteous he will surely live,
and he so trusts in his righteousness that he commits iniquity, none of his righteous deeds will be remembered; but in that same iniquity of his which he has
committed he will die. 14But when I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and he turns from his sin and practices justice and righteousness, 15if a
wicked man restores a pledge, pays back what he has taken by robbery, walks by the statutes which ensure life without committing iniquity, he shall surely live; he shall not die.
16None of his sins that he has committed will be remembered against him. He has practiced justice and righteousness; he shall surely live."

33:10 "say" It is characteristic for an IMPERATIVE (BDB 55, KB 65, Qal IMPERATIVE) to
designate the beginning of YHWH's new message through Ezekiel (i.e. Ezek. 33:10,11,12).

▣ "Surely our transgressions and our sins are upon us, and we are rotting away in them" In chapter 18 the people were blaming their
forefathers for YHWH's judgments, but here in chapter 33 they acknowledge their personal and corporate rebellion.

The phrase "rotting away" is from the curses of Lev. 26:39-42. This phrase is found three times in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 4:17; 24:23; 33:10).

Special Topic: Biblical Faith Is Corporate

▣ "then can we survive" This is literally "live" (BDB 310, KB 309, Qal
IMPERFECT). We must see the devastating mental and physical anguish
that the destruction of Jerusalem caused to the covenant people. Ezekiel, in chapters 33-39
after the destruction of Jerusalem and the temple, begins to reassure the covenant people that
YHWH is still their Covenant God (cf. Isa. 49:14-15) and that He will forgive and restore them,
physically and spiritually (cf. Ezek. 37:11-14).

33:11 "'As I live!' declares the Lord God" This is an oath related to
the name of the Covenant God, YHWH, from the Hebrew VERB "to be." It is the ever-living,
only-living God who swears by His own life (cf. Ezek. 5:11).

Special Topic: Names for Deity, D.

Special Topic: Life (zoē)

▣ "I take no pleasure in the death of the wicked" This is a repetition of Ezek. 18:23,32. The heart of God is love, not judgment
(cf. Exod. 34:6-7; John 3:16; Matt. 11:28-30). God wants all human beings made in His image and likeness to turn and respond to Him (cf. John 3:16;
4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; 1 John 2:1; 4:14) by repentance and faith (cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 2:38,41; 3:16,19; 20:21).

Special Topic: Characteristics of Israel's God (OT)

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

Special Topic: Seek the Lord

▣ "turn from his way and live. Turn back, turn back from your evil ways! Why will you die, Oh house of Israel" The VERB
(BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERTAIVE) is repeated for emphasis (cf. Ezek. 3:19,20; 14:6 [thrice]; 18:21,23,24,26,27,28,30 [twice],32;
33:9,11 [twice],12,14,19). This is a choice humans must make (cf. Deut. 30:1,15,19). Repentance is a crucial spiritual requirement.

Repentance primarily is a turning from self and a turning to God. The Hebrew word (BDB 996) speaks of a change of action, while
the Greek speaks of a change of mind. Both are involved (cf. Ezek. 18:31; Jer. 31:33; also note 2 Cor. 7:8-11).

Special Topic: Repentance (OT)

Special Topic: Repentance (NT)

▣ "house of Israel" Israel in this context refers specifically to Judah. Ezekiel uses this
designation to foreshadow the coming unity of the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

33:12 "The righteousness of the righteous man will not deliver him in the day of his transgression" This
does not refer to cumulative guilt or acquired merit (cf. chapter 18), but lifestyle relational faith! What
a terrible warning! What a wonderful invitation (cf. Ezek. 33:10)!

Special Topic: Righteousness.

33:13 "and he will surely live" This is the INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and the IMPERFECT VERB
of the same root (BDB 310, KB 309, cf. Ezek. 33:15,16), which expresses intensity or emphasis (see note at Ezek. 33:8).

▣ "and he so trusts in his righteousness" This is always a danger of religious humanity. The believer must trust in God,
not in oneself or one's performance. His/her trust (BDB 105) must issue from an initial faith and repentance to an ongoing faith and repentance.
Biblical faith is a daily relationship! Obedience does make a difference (cf. Ezek. 33:16,31-32; Deut. 4:1; Hab. 2:4; Eph. 1:4; 2:8-10; James 2:14-26)
and is the natural result of a dynamic faith.

Special Topic: Covenant

Special Topic: Keep

33:14 "practices justice and righteousness" Notice that there is no distinction in this context between secular and sacred because
all belongs to God. This is a truth that moderns need to hear. All life and all relationships are sacred because of Gen. 1:26-27. We must not
separate justification from sanctification.

Special Topic: Judge, Judgment, Justice

33:15 "restores a pledge" This term, "a pledge," (BDB 286, KB 285) basically means "to bind." When one borrows he is obligated to repay.
To secure this repayment (without interest to a fellow Israelite) the creditor could take something of value and hold it.

- grinding stone, Ezek. 24:6

- garments, Ezek. 24:17; Exod. 22:25-27; Job 24:7,10

- ancestral land and houses, Neh. 5:3 (possibly Job 24:2)

- an essential animal, Job 24:3

- essential help, the children, Exod. 21:7; Lev. 25:39-43; 2 Kgs. 4:1; Job 24:9

Each of these items was a necessary part of daily agricultural existence. To remove any one of these jeopardized the family, even
life itself. YHWH's compassion and care for Israel was to be emulated by those Israelites who had resources. God would bless them for their compassion.
They would be given more so that they could share more (cf. Ezek. 33:13; 2 Cor. 9:6-10).

Special Topic: Wealth

▣ "pays back what he has taken by robbery" Robbery is discussed in Exod. 22:1-4; Lev. 6:4,5. The
stolen items must be returned with a penalty.

Special Topic: Stealing

▣ "walks by the statutes" The VERB (BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT) is an idiom
of lifestyle faith. Faith is personal and communal. The first can be seen and evaluated by how we treat others!

Notice that the statutes of God are meant to bestow life (another INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and IMPERFECT
VERB of the same root, BDB 310, KB 309). God's laws were to protect humanity during this period of fallenness (i.e. Deut. 30:16).

Special Topic: Terms for God's Revelation

Special Topic: The Path, The Way

Special Topic: The Fall of Mankind

33:16 "None of his sins that he has committed will be remembered against him" What a tremendous promise of the forgiveness
of YHWH (cf. Ezek. 18:22; Ps. 103:12; Isa. 1:18; 38:17; 43:25; 44:22; Micah 7:18, 19)! When God forgives, God forgets!

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:17-20

17"Yet your fellow citizens say, 'The way of the Lord is not right,' when it is their own way that is not right.
18When the righteous turns from his righteousness and commits iniquity, then he shall die in it. 19But when the wicked turns from his wickedness
and practices justice and righteousness, he will live by them. 20Yet you say, 'The way of the Lord is not right.' O house of Israel, I will judge each of you according to his ways."

33:17-20 This supposed dialogue between YHWH's spokesperson and the wicked is similar to the diatribe
format found in Malachi, Paul's writings, and 1 John.

A statement of truth is made, then a supposed contemporary objector restates or challenges the first statement. In a
concluding statement from the first speaker, God gives His answer to contemporary false views.

33:17 "The way of the Lord" This speaks of lifestyle faith (i.e. Deut. 3:33; 8:6; 10:12; 11:22; 19:9;
26:17; 28:9; 30:16). The early church's title was "The Way" (cf. Acts 9:2; 18:25,26; 19:9,23; 22:4; 24:14,22).

Special Topic: The Path, The Way

▣ "right" This refers to a measuring standard (BDB 1067). It is used often in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 18:25 [twice], 29 [twice]; 33:17 [twice], 20).
They were claiming that YHWH's justice was unfair (weighted falsely, cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; Prov. 16:2; 24:12), but the problem was human, willful rebellion (cf. Ezek. 18:25, 29).

Special Topic: Righteousness

33:20 "I will judge each of you according to his ways" Notice the individual emphasis continues (i.e. Deut. 24:16; Jer. 31:29-30;
Ezek. 3:16-21; 18; 33). This is a recurrent biblical truth. We reap what we sow!

Note Job 34:11; Ps. 28:4; 62:12; Prov. 24:12; Eccl. 12:14; Jer. 17:10; 32:19; Matt. 16:27; 25:31-46; Rom. 2:6; 14:12; 1 Cor. 3:8;
2 Cor. 5:10; Gal. 6:7-10; 2 Tim. 4:14; 1 Pet. 1:17; Rev. 2:23; 20:12; 22:12!

Special Topic: Judge, Judgment, Justice

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:21-22

21Now in the twelfth year of our exile, on the fifth of the tenth month, the refugees from Jerusalem
came to me, saying, "The city has been taken." 22Now the hand of the Lord had been upon me in the evening, before the
refugees came. And He opened my mouth at the time they came to me in the morning; so my mouth was opened and I was no longer speechless.

33:21 "in the twelfth year of our exile" The Syriac translation (Peshitta) has "eleventh." The Septuagint has "tenth." The exact date is uncertain.

This is one of several dates in Ezekiel that seem to mark the beginning of a new prophetic revelation from YHWH. If this is correct,
then the next date is found in Ezek. 40:1, which implies Ezek. 33:21-39:29 is a unified literary unit. This section of Ezekiel emphasizes the promise of
divine restoration of a segment of the seed of Abraham (see Special Topic: The Remnant [three senses]).

The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1107, identifies several separate oracles in this literary unit.

- 33:21-33

- 34:1-31

- 35:1-36:15

- 36:16-37:14

- 37:15-28

- 38:1-39:39

▣ "The city has been taken" Ezekiel had predicted this earlier, but this was the first eyewitness confirmation. This is a crucial
point in Ezekiel's ministry. Once the predicted judgment of YHWH has struck (i.e. the destruction of Jerusalem), Ezekiel then begins to proclaim
YHWH's messages of hope and restoration.

33:22 "the hand of the Lord had been upon me" This is an idiomatic way of referring to YHWH's initiation
of a revelatory message (cf. Ezek. 1:3; 3:14,22; 8:1; 37:1; 40:1). The phrase usually marks crucial transition points, but here and in chapter 3 it denotes an incoming message.

Special Topic: God Described As Human

Special Topic: Inspiration

▣ "He opened my mouth" Previously, Ezekiel had been forced to do dramatic
actions because he could not speak, but now he was permitted to speak (cf. Ezek. 3:26, 27; 24:27).

23Then the word of the Lord came to me saying, 24"Son of man,
they who live in these waste places in the land of Israel are saying, 'Abraham was only one, yet he possessed the land; so to us who are many the land has been given
as a possession.' 25Therefore say to them, 'Thus says the Lord God, "You eat meat with the blood in it, lift up your
eyes to your idols as you shed blood. Should you then possess the land? 26You rely on your sword, you commit abominations and each of you defiles his neighbor's

in the waste places will fall by the sword, and whoever is in the open field I will give to the beasts to be devoured, and those who are in the strongholds and in the caves will die
of pestilence. 28I will make the land a desolation and a waste, and the pride of her power will cease; and the mountains of Israel will be desolate so that no one will
pass through. 29Then they will know that I am the Lord, when I make the land a desolation and a waste because of all their abominations
which they have committed."'

33:24 "they who live in these waste places in the land of Israel are saying" Those who escaped the captivity and exile to Neo-Babylon (cf. Jeremiah 24),
were asserting that YHWH had blessed them and had cursed the exiles, but this was simply not the case (cf. Ezek. 33:27; 11:1-27).

33:25 "You eat meat with blood in it" This refers to

- the improper preparations of meat (cf. Lev. 3:17; 7:26-27; 17:10,12,14; 19:26; Deut. 12:16, 23; 15:23). In this context it probably
refers to cultic meals at pagan altars.

- This may refer to Canaanite divination (see IVP Bible Background Commentary [OT], p. 721).

▣ "lift up your eyes" This is imagery for prayer. They were idolaters.

▣ "you shed blood" This refers to

- the killing of righteous people

- the killing of the poor

- the offering of their children to the Phoenician fertility god, Molech (see Special Topic: Molech)

▣ "Should you then possess the land" This question is very similar to Jeremiah's temple
sermon of chapter 7, in particular Ezek. 33:9 and 10. YHWH's covenant with Abraham's seed was conditional. This is a crucial theolgocial point!

Special Topic: Covenant

33:26 "You rely on your sword" They were trusting in their military power and walled cities (cf. Ezek. 33:28, "the pride of her power will cease").

▣ "you commit abominations and each of you defiles his neighbor's wife" This refers to the fertility rites of the Canaanite gods, Ba'al and Ashterah.

Special Topic: Fertility Worship of the ANE

Special Topic: Abomination (OT)

33:27-29 These curses reflect Lev. 26:22,25.

33:29 The Jewish Study Bible, p. 1108, says this verse summarizes the message of the whole book.

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 33:30-33

30"But as for you, son of man, your fellow citizens who talk about you by the walls and in the doorways
of the houses, speak to one another, each to his brother, saying, 'Come now and hear what the message is which comes forth from the Lord.' 31They
come to you as people come, and sit before you as My people and hear your words, but they do not do them, for they do the lustful desires expressed
by their mouth, and their heart goes after their gain. 32Behold, you are to them like a sensual song by one who has a beautiful voice and plays well
on an instrument; for they hear your words but they do not practice them. 33So when it comes to pass - as surely it will - then they will know
that a prophet has been in their midst."

33:30 Ezekiel's fellow exiles were talking about (his prophecies) what happened to Jerusalem and
what would happen to the few who remained. In this context the prophet is commanded to address their concerns.

- come ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL

- hear ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL

YHWH still wants to speak to His people. The ones in exile are the people He will begin again with.

33:31 "They come to you as people come, and they sit before you as My people but they do the
lustful desires expressed by their mouth, and their heart goes after their gain" There was
outward, religious show, but no true piety. To them Ezekiel was the best show in town (cf. Ezek. 33:32),
but they had no real desire to turn to YHWH (cf. Isa. 6:9-13; 29:13).

33:32 "for they hear your words but they do not practice them" They hear, but they do not do (i.e. the opposite of shema; see
Special Topic: Listen/Hear [shema]). This is the condemnation of "religious people," cf. Matt. 7:24-27; James 1:23-25).

The exiles loved to come hear or observe Ezekiel's messages, but they did not really believe them. He was the only show in town. This
would all change with the news brought by an exiled survivor of Jerusalem that indeed all that Ezekiel had predicted had occurred (cf. Ezek. 33:33).

Special Topic: Keep

33:33 The mark of a true prophet is that what they predict (unless repentance occurs, i.e. Jonah) comes to pass (cf. Ezek. 33:29;
13:6; Deut. 18:22; Jer. 28:9). Ezekiel had been right about Judah and Jerusalem and he would be right about the destruction of the nations! He would also
be right about the forgiveness and restoration to come!

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the significance of chapters 18 and 33?

- What is the difference between the attitude of the people in chapters 18 and 33?

- Explain the spiritual relationship described in Ezek. 33:12, 13.

- What is repentance?
